# AI Actually, by Anthony Proctor

> Honest, plain-language help for regular people and families to protect themselves from AI that is used against them: AI scam calls and voice clones, AI tools that act without approval, and kids and AI chatbots. Written for the adults (roughly 35 to 64) looking out for older parents and kids.

## What this is

A small independent site. It gives practical steps a family can take tonight, grounded in FBI and FTC guidance, with sources linked. The tips and the guide are free. The only paid thing linked is the author's book on putting AI to work, sold on Amazon.

## Three topics

- **Scam calls and deepfakes.** Voice clones that sound like someone you love. Steps: agree on a family code word, hang up and call back on a number you know, treat gift cards, crypto, wire transfers and payment apps as a stop sign.
- **AI tools doing things you never approved.** Surprise charges and privacy. Check what your AI apps can do without asking, and switch off what you did not mean to allow.
- **Kids and AI chatbots.** Many teens use AI companions. Talk first, rules second.

## Sources used on the site

- FBI IC3 2025 Internet Crime Report: https://www.ic3.gov/AnnualReport/Reports/2025_IC3Report.pdf (22,364 AI-related complaints with adjusted losses over $893 million; people 60+ reported $7.7 billion in losses of all kinds).
- FBI public service announcement, December 2024: https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2024/PSA241203
- FTC on family emergency scams: https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2023/03/scammers-use-ai-enhance-their-family-emergency-schemes
- Common Sense Media on teens and AI companions: https://www.commonsensemedia.org/press-releases/nearly-3-in-4-teens-have-used-ai-companions-new-national-survey-finds
